summary.text: For a typical customer (in West Virginia, area code 415, with no international or voice-mail plan, one call to customer service and median usage, such as about 180 daytime minutes), having an international plan clearly raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves from about 1% to about 20%.

For the 805 of 4000 customers that one usage part acts on, that part clearly raises it: for a typical such customer (in Alabama, with about 240 daytime minutes costing about $41 and 238 evening minutes) from about 5% to about 19%, and a higher evening charge clearly raises it for that customer from about 5% to about 45%.
Daytime minutes clearly add to it only once they rise above about 233: going from 0 to 271 minutes moves a typical customer from about 1% to about 8%.

For a typical customer that a service-call part acts on (in Idaho, with three calls to customer service and about 143 daytime minutes costing about $24), going from 0 to 3 calls clearly raises it from about 2% to about 9%, and a higher daytime charge clearly lowers it from about 9% to about 2%.
Being in California instead of West Virginia raises it to about 8% (on the training data only).
The model ignores the number of daytime, evening and international calls, total international minutes and total night-time minutes.

parts.name: churn_model
parts.original_hypothesis: Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.348 + linear_backbone + heavy_day_eve_usage + service_call_gate + day_charge_no_voicemail + csc_hinge + eve_charge_brake + state_offsets), additive in logit; the top-level children never feed each other (the heavy-usage hinge 1694 is split, with copy 1694_b inside the gate). The output also reads csc_escalation.10379 (the state:46 unit, grandchild exit) with weight -0.005. 30 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, 4000 rows, local in-memory forward passes): full AUC 0.9193; all nonlinear children replaced by least-squares linear fits on their entries 0.8303 (jointly 0.8297; refit L2 logistic regression 0.8433). Restoring one child's nonlinearity alone onto the linearised model gains: service_call_gate +0.064, day_charge_no_voicemail +0.046, heavy_day_eve_usage +0.045, csc_hinge +0.007, eve_charge_brake -0.002. Shapley split of the gain: gate 0.041, day-charge 0.023, heavy-usage 0.022. Removing all state effects drops AUC to 0.9094 (0.010). SHAP top features: day minutes/charge, service calls, international plan, voicemail, eve charge.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: service_call_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Many customer-service calls AND low usage -> churn. 997 = relu(0.389*CSC + 0.494*csc_escalation.7689 - 1.718*usage_brake.4397 + 0.206*usage_brake.1694_b - 0.641), readout +3.108. The convex service-call signal pushes 997 up; the usage ramp 4397 shuts it for anyone with average or higher day usage. Mean contribution: 0 for 0-2 calls at any usage; at 3 calls +1.25 logit below 150 day minutes, +0.6 at 150-180; at 4 calls +4.0 / +2.6 / +0.9 (below 150 / 150-180 / 180-200 minutes); at 5 calls +7.0 / +4.4 / +2.6; at 6+ calls +10.7 / +8.5 / +5.5; about 0 above 220 minutes except for 6+ calls. Train churn with 4+ calls and under 150 day minutes is 87-100% (86 rows) vs 4-6% for 0-3 calls. Rare-state switches inside the gate: state:35 removes the usage brake (via 20866), so 9 of its 87 rows with 3+ calls get +0.5 to +6.8 logit (only 3 of the 9 churned); state:46 lowers the service-call signal (via 10379), so its high-call rows lose up to 2 more logit. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.8945 (linear-fit R^2 0.35); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8939 (gain +0.064). Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: linear_backbone
parts.original_hypothesis: Sparse linear backbone: 30 inputs summed at identity node lin_agg (read out by the output with weight 1). In raw units: internationalPlan +2.94 logit for plan holders; totalIntlCharge +0.51 per dollar; totalDayMinutes -0.0075 per minute (-2.6 logit across the range; the day-usage hinges override it above about 200 minutes); totalNightCharge +0.10 per dollar; voiceMailPlan -0.70; accountLength +0.0036 per day; totalEveMinutes +0.0026 per minute. numberCustomerServiceCalls has almost no linear term here (-0.015 per call): its whole effect runs through the service-call gate and hinge. 20 state one-hots enter directly; their z-scored in-state value is 7-10, so small weights are large per-state offsets: state:11 -2.44 logit (73 rows, 3 churners), state:46 -1.71, state:31 -1.53 (cancelled by unit 2016), state:4 +1.52 (41 rows), state:26 +0.88, state:38 -0.66, state:43 +0.51. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: usage_brake
parts.original_hypothesis: Two usage signals feeding the service-call gate 997. 4397 = relu(0.653*dayCharge + 1.327*15054 + 0.578*23191 - 0.804*20866 - 0.502), with 15054 = relu(1.483*dayCharge + 0.998*eveCharge + 1.089) and 23191 = relu(1.007*dayCharge - 1.567): a convex, increasing ramp in day charge (and to a lesser extent evening charge), zero only for low-usage customers; it enters 997 with weight -1.718, i.e. it is a brake that shuts the gate for heavy users. 20866 = relu(1.01*state:35 - 0.317) is on only in state:35 (value 6.45) and removes the brake there (4397 in-state mean 0.15 vs 1.77): a rare-state switch. 1694_b is the split copy of the heavy-usage hinge 1694 (same function as in heavy_day_eve_usage) entering 997 with weight +0.206. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably.

parts.name: heavy_day_eve_usage
parts.original_hypothesis: Hinge on combined day+evening usage, read out twice. 1694 = relu(1.127*dayMinutes + 0.763*eveCharge - 0.009*state:27 + 0.012*28715 - 1.121) (z-scored), readout +2.03; 3237 = relu(0.871*1694 - 0.478), readout +1.05, makes the hinge steeper (convex) once 1694 exceeds 0.55. 28715 = relu(0.811 + 1.234*state:35 + 1.001*11600) and 11600 = relu(1.011*state:20 - 2.214) are state dribbles whose effect through the 0.012 weight is under 0.11 logit; state:27 shifts the threshold by at most -0.2 logit. Mean contribution is 0 unless both day and evening usage are well above average: +1.2 logit at 200-220 day and 250-300 eve minutes, +2.6 at 220-250/250-300, +4.3 at 250-280/250-300, +6.6 at 280+/250-300 and +8.3 when day > 280 and eve > 300 (train churn 60-72% in the heavy cells, vs 3-12% below 200 day minutes). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.9131 (linear-fit R^2 0.40); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8749 (gain +0.045). Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.

parts.name: csc_escalation
parts.original_hypothesis: Convex customer-service-call signal for the gate. 30505 = relu(0.837*CSC - 0.671) (on from 2 calls), 7689 = relu(0.897*CSC + 0.9*30505 - 0.247*10379 + 0.143): about 0 at 0 calls, rising ~0.7 per call to 2 calls and ~1.4 per call above. 10379 = relu(0.865*state:46 - 0.359*state:22 - 1.256*state:9 - 0.958) is on only in state:46 (80 rows, value 5.3); it lowers 7689 by 1.3 there (so the gate fires less for state:46 high-call customers) and has a negligible direct readout (-0.005). state:22 and state:9 only push 10379 further below zero (no effect).
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: day_charge_no_voicemail
parts.original_hypothesis: 2899 = relu(0.614*dayCharge - 0.963*vmailMessages - 0.027*CSC - 0.753) (z-scored), readout +3.66: high day charge raises churn only for customers with no voicemail messages. For no-voicemail customers the mean contribution is about 0 below 200 day minutes, +1.45 logit at 220-250, +2.74 at 250-280 and +4.34 above 280 (train churn 21%, 49%, 84%); for customers with any voicemail messages it is 0 (at most +0.1), matching their low churn (0-12%) even at high day usage. Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: state_offsets
parts.original_hypothesis: Hidden units fed only by state one-hots. The categories are mutually exclusive, so the block is exactly a per-state logit offset table (its linear fit has R^2 = 1). 2016 = relu(1.581 - 1.551*state:31), readout -1.41: on outside state 31, off inside it, so state:31 gets +2.57 logit, cancelling most of the backbone's -1.53 (net +1.04, 90 rows, 22 churners). 32834 = relu(1.007*state:47 - 0.354), readout +0.171: state:47 +1.21 (72 rows, 21 churners). 827 = relu(1.057*state:12 - 0.665), readout +0.061: state:12 +0.51 (55 rows, 6 churners). 3620 = relu(1.013*state:49 - 1.236), readout -0.074: state:49 -0.33. 6606 = relu(0.231*state:0 + 0.092*8711 + 0.156) is always on, with 8711 = relu(0.511*state:49 - 0.076*state:48 - 0.849*9229 + 1.19) and 9229 = relu(0.271*20866 - 0.903), 20866 = relu(1.01*state:35 - 0.317): a linear chain giving small offsets, state:0 -0.38, state:49 -0.05, state:48 +0.01, state:35 +0.01 (readout -0.192). Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.9193 (linear-fit R^2 1.00); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8303 (gain +0.000). Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.

parts.name: eve_charge_brake
parts.original_hypothesis: 19579 = relu(1.025*eveCharge + 1.015*23438 - 1.052), 23438 = relu(1.047*eveCharge - 0.386); readout -0.256. A convex function of evening charge alone with a negative readout: 0 below 220 evening minutes, -0.03 logit at 220-250, -0.29 at 250-280, -0.71 above 280. It slightly flattens the evening part of the heavy-usage hinge for customers whose day usage is not high; its AUC contribution is nil (linearising it changes train AUC by -0.0005). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.9188 (linear-fit R^2 0.49); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8281 (gain -0.002). Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.

parts.name: csc_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: 21178 = relu(0.808*CSC - 0.887), readout +0.324: a small hinge on customer service calls, 0 for 0-3 calls, +0.20 logit at 4, +0.40 at 5 and +0.69 at 6+ calls, independent of usage. reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
